item.title: Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) for Tariffs and Supply Chains: Pathways to Resilient Economic Planning
item.content:encoded:

The collection seeks to explore how MCDA approaches can inform policy decisions and strategies for building more resilient economic systems in the face of global trade complexities and supply chain disruptions.

item.title: Benchmarking Adaptive Supply Chains: Performance Metrics, Maturity Models, and Socio-Technical Configurations
item.content:encoded:
Aamir Rashid, City University of New York

Rizwana Rasheed, City University of New York

Organizations face ongoing disruptions and must adapt their supply chains while managing sustainability and digital transformation. However, there is limited frameworks for measuring and comparing adaptive supply chain performance across different organizations and contexts. This special issue seeks to advance research that uses benchmarking logic to systematically evaluate how well supply chains adapt.

The special issue emphasizes understanding adaptive performance through the interaction of people, technology, governance, and sustainability practices. Rather than treating adaptation as a general concept, research should operationalize adaptability with measurable constructs and benchmarking frameworks that highlight performance differences between configurations.

Contributions should employ rigorous comparative designs using quantitative, qualitative, or mixed methods to benchmark adaptive supply chains across industries and countries. By identifying which configurations perform better and under what conditions, the research will provide actionable insights for practitioners and policymakers.

Appel publié par Benchmarking: An International Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Performance frontiers and efficiency analysis of adaptive supply chains
  • Cross-country and institutional benchmarking of supply chain adaptability
  • Governance, collaboration, and coordination as benchmarked performance drivers
  • Comparative analysis of sustainability and resilience performance trade-offs

item.title: Sustainable Paths in Digital Supply Chains: Navigating Environmental Challenges and Technological Frontiers
item.content:encoded:
Harshad Sonar, Indian Institute of Management Sambalpur

Bishal Dey Sarkar, Indian Institute of Management Bodhgaya

Sandeep Jagtap, Lund University

Hana Trollman, University of Leicester

This special issue examines how digital technologies can be integrated with sustainability objectives in modern supply chains. Organizations are increasingly pressured to reduce environmental impacts and ensure ethical operations while managing technological disruption. The issue explores how emerging tools like artificial intelligence, blockchain, and data analytics can enhance supply chain transparency, efficiency, emissions monitoring, and resilience while addressing climate risks and regulatory demands.

The collection seeks empirical, conceptual, and methodological contributions that bridge theory and practice in digital sustainability transitions. It recognizes that technological adoption alone is insufficient; successful transformation requires supportive leadership, training, and organizational culture change. The special issue draws on multiple theoretical perspectives to provide comprehensive understanding of how human and organizational factors influence sustainability-driven digitalization across different organizational contexts.

item.title: Decision Support Systems for Sustainable and Resilient Transitions
item.content:encoded:
Femi Olan, University of Essex

Uchitha Jayawickrama, Loughborough University

Shaofeng Liu, University of Plymouth

This special issue seeks high-quality research on Decision Support Systems (DSS) that address sustainable and resilient transitions across organisations, societies, and supply chains. In environments characterised by technological disruption, environmental threats, and changing workforce demands, DSS models, frameworks, tools, and applications are essential for enabling evidence-based decision-making and strategic adaptation.

The call welcomes contributions exploring both theoretical foundations and practical applications of DSS across four main areas: green and sustainable transitions, digital transformation, workforce and skills transitions, and resilient supply chains. Submissions should demonstrate how DSS support organisations and societies in balancing efficiency with sustainability and resilience objectives while navigating rapid change.

Relevant submissions include conceptual models, quantitative frameworks with performance indicators, empirical case studies, interdisciplinary approaches, and critical analyses of adoption barriers and governance considerations for DSS implementation in transitions.

Appel publié par Journal of Decision Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • DSS for Workforce and Skills Transitions: DSS for workforce re-skilling, hybrid work planning, and change management
  • DSS for Resilient Supply Chains, Organisations and Societies: DSS frameworks for supply chain mapping, disruption visibility, dynamic reconfiguration, organisational learning and society regeneration

item.title: Global Supply Chain Reconfiguration Under Tariff Uncertainty
item.content:encoded:
Guoqing Zhang, University of Windsor

Jiaguo Liu, Dalian Maritime University

Hakan Yildiz, Wayne State University

This special issue addresses the urgent challenge of reconfiguring global supply chains in response to escalating tariff uncertainty and shifting trade policies. The unprecedented complexity of current tariff environments, characterized by high rates, retaliatory measures, and trade tensions, demands new decision-making approaches to support practical supply chain management.

The special issue seeks high-quality research that applies Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence methods to tackle these challenges. Contributions should include theoretical developments, methodological innovations, and applied modeling studies with real-world relevance, particularly those integrating OR, AI, supply chain management, and international economics.

item.title: International Business in a Reconfiguring Southeast Asia
item.content:encoded:
S. Tamer Cavusgil, Georgia State University

Marleen Dieleman, IMD Business School

Md. Tareq Hossain, Thammasat University

Ruey-Jer "Bryan" Jean, National Taiwan University

Destan Kandemir, Georgia State University

Suntichai Kotcharin, Thammasat University

Hussain Rammal, Adelaide University

Southeast Asia represents a significant yet theoretically under-explored region in international business research. With ten ASEAN economies forming the world's fifth-largest economic bloc and attracting substantial foreign investment, the region presents unique phenomena including supply chain reconfiguration driven by China-plus-one strategies, the emergence of regional multinationals, and institutional diversity across countries with different political systems and development stages.

Despite its empirical importance, Southeast Asia remains underrepresented in leading international management journals, where research focuses predominantly on China and India. This special issue seeks contributions that treat Southeast Asian phenomena as theoretically generative rather than merely illustrative. It particularly encourages submissions from scholars based in the region and aims to develop international management theory beyond existing BRICS-centric frameworks by leveraging the region's distinctive features including family capitalism, ethnic-Chinese business networks, state-linked enterprises, and ASEAN-level institutional structures.

Appel publié par Management International Review. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • The rise and internationalization of Southeast Asian multinationals, including digital-native champions, conglomerate-based regional players, and state-linked enterprises
  • Supply-chain reconfiguration, maritime connectivity, and regional supply-chain governance in Vietnam, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and the Philippines
  • Cross-border trade, geopolitics, and strategies of Southeast Asian firms hedging between major power blocs
  • Indigenous theorizing and methodological innovation drawing on Southeast Asian intellectual traditions and fieldwork methods

item.title: Digitalization for responsive and circular supply chains
item.content:encoded:
Günter Prockl, Copenhagen Business School

Alexander Pflaum, University of Bamberg

Haozhe Chen, Iowa State University

Marcel Papert, University of Bamberg

Modern supply chains face unprecedented disruptions while simultaneously confronting environmental limits and resource scarcity. This requires a fundamental transformation toward more responsive and circular systems. Digital technologies including IoT, AI, digital twins, and blockchain are critical enablers for building resilient supply chains that adapt quickly to change while reducing resource consumption and closing material loops.

The special issue seeks papers demonstrating how digital and data-driven solutions implement these responsive and circular supply chains, along with their associated business models. Contributions should explore digital technologies across multiple supply chain tiers, with particular emphasis on industry-specific applications and the integration of responsiveness, servitization, and sustainability goals.

item.title: Celebrating the 75th Birthday of Professor Kathryn E. Stecke
item.content:encoded:
Bernie F. Quiroga, West Virginia University

Xuying Zhao, Texas A&M University

Oleg Gusikhin, Ford Motor Company

Andrea Matta, Politecnico di Milano

Yong Yin, Doshisha Business School

This special issue honors Professor Kathryn E. Stecke's 75th birthday by showcasing research that builds upon her substantial contributions to production research, flexible manufacturing systems, supply chain management, and the interface between production and marketing. The issue seeks to curate cutting-edge articles in active and emerging areas that reflect her legacy and influence.

The special issue welcomes high-quality submissions including empirical studies, analytical models, simulation-based research, case analyses, and conceptual papers. Manuscripts should demonstrate rigorous, impactful research with comprehensive literature reviews, novel decision-aid models, comparisons with state-of-the-art methods, discussions of real-life applications, and managerial insights.

Appel publié par International Journal of Production Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Advances in flexible manufacturing systems (FMSs), including machine grouping, loading policies, and production ratio optimization for enhanced utilization
  • Interfaces between production and marketing, including focal points such as advance selling strategies, pre-order mechanisms considering consumer behavior (e.g., loss aversion), lead time and price quotation modes, production-transportation integration in make-to-order systems, and competition/coordination in online marketplaces
  • Reconfigurable production systems, such as Seru, for improving responsiveness and adaptability in volatile environments
  • Supply chain resilience strategies, including adaptive ordering, disruption mitigation, and multi-echelon network design amid geopolitical and operational uncertainties
  • Production planning and scheduling in capital-intensive systems with machine flexibility, focusing on hierarchical approaches and real-time control
  • Integration of digital technologies (e.g., AI, digital twins, and data analytics) in manufacturing and supply chains to boost efficiency and cost control
  • Empirical analyses of manufacturing efficiencies in sectors like semiconductors, automotive, and electronics, drawing on case studies of disruption responses
  • Comparative studies of traditional vs. innovative production methods, such as Toyota Production System vs. Seru, with emphasis on performance metrics

item.title: Hétérodoxie logistique : explorer des chemins de traverse
item.content:encoded:
Adèle Fouché, Université de Tours

François Fulconis, Avignon Université

Gilles Paché, Aix-Marseille Université

La logistique et le supply chain management sont actuellement dominés par des approches normatives et techniques privilégiant l'optimisation de la performance. Cette normalisation risque de rendre invisibles certaines pratiques, acteurs et dynamiques fondamentalement logistiques. Le numéro spécial propose d'explorer une hétérodoxie logistique : une démarche scientifique interrogeant les angles morts du champ, déplaçant les cadres d'analyse existants et ouvrant de nouvelles perspectives pour appréhender la logistique comme fait social traversé par des enjeux historiques, politiques et culturels.

Cette approche envisage la logistique au-delà de la gestion des flux licites et visibles, incluant les terrains « sensibles » ou « hors normes » : économies informelles, réseaux parallèles, circulations illicites et systèmes clandestins. Ces contextes offrent des espaces empiriques pour comprendre la matérialité des flux, les formes alternatives de coordination et les logiques de pouvoir structurant les chaînes logistiques.

Appel publié par Logistique & Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Logistique dans les contextes informels, illégaux ou clandestins

  • Repenser les concepts classiques du supply chain management (performance, résilience, coordination, visibilité) à travers des configurations non-normatives
  • Continuités entre logistiques historiques (esclavage, colonisation) et systèmes contemporains
  • Organisation des flux dans des environnements contraints, incertains ou hostiles
  • Rôle des infrastructures, institutions et technologies dans les systèmes alternatifs

  • Construction et recomposition des frontières entre licite et illicite dans les chaînes logistiques
  • Implications éthiques, politiques et sociétales de l'hétérodoxie logistique
  • Renouvellement des cadres théoriques et méthodologiques en logistique

item.title: Low-Altitude Logistics: Theoretical Frameworks, Underlying Mechanisms and Scenario-Based Applications
item.content:encoded:
Weihua Liu, Tianjin University

Lei Xu, Civil Aviation University of China

Kannan Govindan, Adelaide University

Yang Cheng, Aalborg University

Low-altitude logistics, enabled by drones and digital platforms integrated with ground transportation systems, represents an emerging frontier in logistics and supply chain management. While existing research has explored drone-assisted delivery and truck-drone coordination, significant gaps remain between rapid real-world experimentation and fragmented academic understanding. The special issue addresses critical questions about adoption barriers, network integration, stakeholder acceptance, business model viability, and sustainability implications of low-altitude logistics systems.

The journal invites empirically grounded studies that develop theoretical frameworks, uncover underlying mechanisms, and examine scenario-based applications of low-altitude logistics. Research should explain how organizations adopt and govern these systems, how they reshape logistics networks and service processes, and how they affect operational efficiency, resilience, sustainability, and public value. The special issue seeks to establish a coherent research agenda moving beyond isolated technological applications.

item.title: Net-Zero Pathways in Logistics, Transportation, and Supply Chain Management
item.content:encoded:
Paul Tae-Woo Lee, Zhejiang University

International organizations have implemented regulations requiring decarbonization of transportation and logistics industries. The special issue addresses net-zero emissions implementation through multimodal transport networks, where major cargo owners and stakeholders have committed to zero-emission transportation. AI and big data technologies are identified as catalysts for digital transformation and carbon reduction optimization.

The special issue aims to fill research gaps concerning net-zero pathway implementation, particularly around three key challenges: direct emissions reduction, higher capital and operating costs for green technologies, and establishing sustainable green energy supply chains. The collection seeks comprehensive and integrated approaches to enable logistics and transportation industries to achieve carbon reduction and multimodal network sustainability.

Researchers are invited to explore how AI, digitalization, new technologies, and policy mechanisms can support decarbonization. The special issue targets the research community and practitioners in transport, logistics, and supply chains to provide managerial insights and expand literature on net-zero pathways.

Appel publié par International Journal of Logistics Research and Applications. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Performance extra-financière et transformation des supply chains : enjeux réglementaires, innovations et défis opérationnels
item.content:encoded:
Elizabeth Couzineau-Zegwaard, PPA Business School

Nathalie Fabbe-Costes, Aix-Marseille Université

Olivier Meier, Université Paris-Est Créteil

This special issue examines how supply chains are being transformed by regulatory pressures and sustainability imperatives. The convergence of resource scarcity, climate urgency, and increasingly stringent European regulations—including CSRD, CSDDD, and the Digital Product Passport—requires companies to integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance into their supply chain strategies. However, this integration raises significant methodological and operational challenges around impact measurement, traceability, and inter-organizational coordination.

The call seeks contributions exploring the tensions and synergies between extra-financial performance requirements and supply chain management from academic, regulatory, and managerial perspectives. Recent regulatory uncertainty, including the proposed Omnibus simplification package, creates new research questions around regulatory path dependency, stranded costs, and the trade-offs between anticipatory compliance and operational greenwashing versus greenhushing strategies.

Appel publié par Logistique & Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Sustainable regulations and supply chain management strategies: impacts of CSRD, CSDDD, and European taxonomy on supply chain structuring and logistics choices (relocation, supplier diversification), integration of ESRS in extra-financial reporting, compliance tools and methodologies
  • Circular economy and innovation: circular business models (reuse, repair, recycling), eco-design levers, contribution of digital technologies (blockchain, AI, IoT) to transition toward more sustainable or regenerative supply chains
  • Measurement, transparency and risks: impact assessment indicators and methodologies (Scope 3, biodiversity, human rights), comparative uses of GRI, SASB and ESRS frameworks, identification of greenwashing signals and best practices for credibilizing ESG commitments, disclosure strategy for objectives versus results in supply chain extra-financial performance
  • Extra-financial performance measurement and supply chain management: impact of extra-financial performance measurement on supply chain design and decisions, trade-offs between cost control, profitability and value creation beyond financial returns, does work on measuring and improving extra-financial performance stimulate logistics innovations?

Timeline

  • November 15, 2026: Manuscript submission deadline

item.title: The Agentic Supply Chain: Entering a new era in AI in Supply Chain Management
item.content:encoded:
Alexandra Brintrup, University of Cambridge

Thomas Choi, Arizona State University

George Huang, Hong Kong Polytechnic University

Dmitry Ivanov, Berlin School of Economics and Law

Recent advances in agentic Large Language Models have created new opportunities for autonomous decision-making in supply chains. This special issue seeks to advance rigorous research on how these AI agents can transform supply chain management by integrating perspectives from operations, AI, complexity science, and industrial engineering. While multi-agent systems have been studied for years, recent LLM breakthroughs now enable more flexible, scalable, and practical implementations that major corporations and technology providers are already exploring.

The special issue welcomes diverse research methodologies including technical solutions, modeling, empirical studies, and experimental work with practical implications. Topics span from using agentic systems for optimization and forecasting to managing risks, designing interorganizational coordination systems, and addressing technical and governance challenges such as trustworthiness, safety, and performance evaluation.

Appel publié par International Journal of Production Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Discourse on utilising agentic systems for complex scenarios in supply chain management: Risk and disruption management, logistics and supply chain optimisation, transportation routes, inventory management, quality control, demand forecasting, and warehouse planning and location, and cash flow predictions
  • Supply network design with agentic technology: Supplier relationship configurations, agentic digital twins to simulate inventory flows, sustainability implications across the supply chain, circular supply chains, supply chain visibility, and supply chain financing
  • Interorganisational agentic systems: Effective multi-agent negotiation and coordination, the design of mediative and persuasive agentic systems, preservation of organisational privacy during multi-agent communication
  • Hybrid systems: Integration of agentic systems with blockchain, IoT, Omniverse, and traditional multi-agent systems
  • Emergence and Complexity: Unintended consequences of agentic deployment at the system scale, governance, trustworthiness and safety, centralised versus decentralised control, human-in-the-loop agentic systems
  • Technical challenges: Performance evaluation, efficient task division, ablation analysis and back testing, sensitivity analysis, agentic architectures operating in high uncertainty environments, long-term horizon reasoning, overcoming hallucinations

Timeline

item.title: Essay Frontiers: A Call for Bold Ideas, New Voices, and New Directions in Logistics and SCM
item.content:encoded:
Maciel Queiroz, FGV EAESP

Morgane Fritz, Excelia Business School

Britta Gammelgaard, University of Southern Denmark

Logistics and supply chain management (L/SCM) have advanced through analytical rigor and empirical refinement. However, the contemporary landscape, shaped by geopolitical shifts, digital transformation, climate pressures, and evolving societal expectations, requires more than incremental extensions of existing models. It calls for a reconsideration of the assumptions, values, and conceptual boundaries that underpin the field. Many of the most pressing challenges in L/SCM today are not only empirical, but also normative, philosophical, and inherently interdisciplinary.

This special issue seeks essays that move beyond established paradigms and offer reflective, provocative, and conceptually grounded perspectives that offer new lenses and open new directions for research and practice. The objective is to complement empirical work by fostering ideas that challenge, reframe, and extend our understanding of L/SCM.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Logistics Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Reshaping Organisations and Supply Chains in a Polycrisis Era: Interdependent Climate, Geopolitical, Economic and Technological Shocks
item.content:encoded:
Hugo Lam, affiliation required but not provided

Over the last decade, managers, policymakers, scholars, and society at large have grappled with an escalating series of interconnected shocks: climate emergencies, geopolitical tensions, economic volatility and rapid technological disruption. What distinguishes the current era is not simply the frequency or severity of these shocks, but their deep interdependence, which is likely to prolong their effects for decades. Climate events often trigger food insecurity that fuels political instability; geopolitical conflict reshapes energy markets and trade flows; and technological breakthrough creates new vulnerabilities even as it may offer new capabilities. These dynamics do not unfold in isolation, but very often interact, amplify one another, and cascade across organisational boundaries and supply chains to impact sectors, regions and continents.
